title: The pH Scale
objective: After this level you can explain the pH scale.
summary: Sorensen gave acidity one number, pH, in 1909. It runs 0 to 14 with 7 neutral, and each step is tenfold: lime juice is about 1,000 times as acidic as coffee.

cards.headline: The pH scale was born in a beer company's laboratory.
cards.body: In 1909 the Danish chemist S.P.L. Sorensen ran the chemistry department at the Carlsberg Laboratory, backed by the brewery of the same name. He needed a simple way to say how acidic something was. His answer is a number you now meet everywhere: pH.

cards.headline: One number from 0 to 14
cards.body: Before Sorensen, there was no widely accepted way to say how acidic a solution was. pH fixed that. The scale usually runs from 0 to 14, and 7 is neutral: pure water. Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic. Lime juice sits around 2 and coffee around 5, while household ammonia is up near 12. One number tells you which side of the line you're on.

cards.headline: Each step is ten times
cards.body: Here's the twist: pH is not like a ruler. Each whole step is a tenfold change, so water at pH 5 is ten times more acidic than water at pH 6. Lime juice at about 2 is three steps below coffee at about 5, which makes it 10 x 10 x 10: about 1,000 times more acidic. Small numbers, big differences.
cards.callout: One pH step = ten times more (or less) acidic.

mascot.line: Three little steps, a thousandfold jump. The pH scale does not do small talk.

cards.headline: Why the numbers run backward
cards.body: Remember Level 61's hydrogen ions? pH is built from how many a solution holds, defined as the negative logarithm of their concentration. The minus sign is why the scale runs backward: the more hydrogen ions, the lower the pH. A low pH means lots of hydrogen ions, a high pH means few.

cards.headline: pH: measured
learned: Sorensen introduced pH in 1909 at the Carlsberg Laboratory
pH 7 is neutral; below is acidic, above is basic
Each pH step is a tenfold change
More hydrogen ions mean a lower pH

questions.prompt: On the pH scale, what does a pH of exactly 7 mean?

options.label: Strongly acidic
options.rationale: Strong acids sit near the bottom of the scale.

options.label: Strongly basic
options.rationale: Strong bases sit near the top of the scale.

options.label: The highest value possible
options.rationale: The scale usually runs up to 14.

questions.explanation: pH 7 is neutral: pure water. Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.

questions.prompt: How many times more acidic is a solution at pH 3 than one at pH 5?

options.label: 2 times
options.rationale: Each step is tenfold, not one more unit.

options.label: 20 times
options.rationale: Tenfold per step means multiplying, not adding.

options.label: 1,000 times
options.rationale: That would be three steps apart, like pH 2 and pH 5.

questions.explanation: Two steps on the pH scale are 10 x 10 = 100 times the acidity.

questions.prompt: Level 61 said acids hand off hydrogen ions. As a solution gains more hydrogen ions, what happens to its pH number?

options.label: It rises toward 14
options.rationale: That is the basic direction, with fewer hydrogen ions.

options.label: It stays at 7 no matter what
options.rationale: Only a neutral solution sits at 7.

options.label: It jumps above 14
options.rationale: More hydrogen ions push pH down, not up.

questions.explanation: pH is the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration, so more hydrogen ions mean a lower pH.
